diagnosis.whyThisWorkerDidNotFixEitherLayer: Both fixes would be this verifier authorising its own read. Widening the LANE_KIND regex edits a shared script outside this lane's owned paths, to admit the very lane whose work it would then permit. Writing a grant into the ledger issues this worker its own claim, and the ledger exists to make ownership provable — Captain's own crossVerificationRules forbid one family having two active verification owners, and the grant is the mechanism that prevents it. Verifying without a grant would leave the ledger unable to say who owns the independent read of these two families, which is exactly what factory check F24 tests. The refusal is doing its job.

whatCaptainNeedsToDo.option B: Admit the XVF prefix in scripts/grade-a-packet-factory-24h/claim.mjs LANE_KIND, then issue the same two grants under XVF-B. This is the larger change because CLOSED_LANE_KINDS and the lane-contract checks read the same vocabulary.
